candidates.label: Acute pericarditis with right ventricular strain
missing_or_uncertain: ECG diffuse ST elevation not clearly described

candidates.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy with right ventricular involvement

response.rationale: The combination of chest pain, ECG changes (ST elevation in V2/V3 and new RBBB), right ventricular dilatation, and elevated pulmonary artery pressure in a young woman with normal coronary arteries strongly suggests acute pulmonary embolism with right heart strain. The absence of dyspnea and syncope does not exclude PE. The treatment with anticoagulants supports this. Other causes of ST elevation and RV strain are less likely given the normal coronaries and lack of typical features.
